\n===== runs/R23/design/WORKFLOW.md =====
7: At the decision time `2026-10-31 18:00 Asia/Shanghai`, produce a frozen plan for `2026-11-01` through `2026-12-12` inclusive: 42 dates × 12 stores × 8 items = 4,032 rows per required table. For each `service_date, store_id, item_id`, deliver a point forecast, a nominal 90% interval, and an integer replenishment quantity. Every daily plan must respect item/store maximum 55, network capacity 1,600 units, and procurement spend 6,000 yuan. The two losses are shortage and waste; procurement is a budget constraint. There is no carryover inventory; unmet demand is lost and leftovers are discarded.
40: | 3. Produce point forecasts | Fit reference `shared_ridge10` and `weekly_median56` independently at each origin. The reference excludes weather and settlement. Alternative features must also obey availability. Keep every origin's input snapshot, code/config hashes, feature lineage, and prediction output. | One keyed point forecast table per `method_id` and origin | Require exact key cardinality (96 per date per method), finite nonnegative predictions, no duplicate/missing keys, and all feature timestamps ≤ origin. On failure, fix only with a versioned change and rerun affected original checks. |
41: | 4. Estimate forecast uncertainty | For each validation origin, retain 96-coordinate daily error vectors against the exact demand report revision available at evaluation time. A vector becomes calibration-eligible only once all 96 labels have arrived; record each label revision/availability and its source forecast origin. Calibration at later origins uses only vectors fully available by that origin. Build marginal lower/upper quantiles for nominal 90% intervals. | `residual_vectors`, `residual_lineage`, keyed `lower90_units`, `upper90_units`, `interval_level=0.9` | If a vector is incomplete, exclude the entire vector from joint scenarios and record why. If no complete vectors exist, no calibrated interval/optimized stochastic plan is available; stop that branch or label a separately authorized provisional rule. Do not silently use partial rows or call a point forecast a 90% interval. |
42: | 5. Optimize daily plan | Use full-day residual vectors as scenarios added to each date's point forecast and clipped at zero. Minimize scenario-average shortage plus waste with integer `q` for each store-item; enforce all 96 item maxima, network capacity, and procurement budget. Compare with the supplied current policy implementation and a clearly defined operational comparator under the same scenarios and constraints. | Keyed plan table, solver record, objective decomposition | Recompute constraints/objective from emitted `q`; reject nonfinite/fractional/negative/over-cap outputs or solver failure. Preserve feasible incumbent, bound, gap, and status; do not call a feasible candidate optimal unless the solver evidence supports that claim. |
44: | 7. Generate 42-day outputs | At the fixed origin `2026-10-31 18:00`, refit the selected eligible method on the final as-of snapshot; create all 4,032 forecast rows and 4,032 plan rows for Nov 1–Dec 12. Forecast and replenishment are separate tables, each key includes method identity. | `future_predictions.csv`, `future_replenishment.csv`, `decision_summary.csv`, lineage and reproduction manifest | Enforce 42×96 unique keys in both tables, same key set/method, finite point/lower/upper values, ordered interval endpoints, exact `interval_level`, integer `q`, and every daily constraint. Future actual demand is never needed or scored. |
53: | `predictions.csv` | `service_date,store_id,item_id,method_id,demand_point_units,lower90_units,upper90_units,interval_level`; 0.9 interval level; finite values; `lower90_units <= upper90_units`; exactly 4,032 unique keys per selected method |
